text:
alex_support: heads up — we got a high-priority customer escalation (cust-774) reporting much worse p99 on generation endpoints since ~03:00 UTC. they say median ok but tail huge.

mike_sre: can you paste the correlation id or sample request? any sudden deploys? :eyes:

alex_support: correlation ids: corr=0a1b2c3d, corr=0a1b2c7f. no deploys in last 6h per deploy-bot. customer included a small repro: a 200-token prompt, concurrency 40, model=rw-large-quant. they say p95 ~150ms -> 200ms, p99 jumps from 300ms -> 800ms.

jena_ml: that pattern screams batching timeouts — large concurrency + model with kv cache churn. i pulled the perf dashboard: for model rw-large-quant in us-west1, p50 ~60ms, p95 ~240ms (up 60ms), p99 ~820ms (huge spike) starting 02:48 UTC. throughput steady.

perf_bot: alert: p99_latency > 700ms on /v1/generate (rw-large-quant) — started 02:48 UTC — affected requests 1724

mike_sre: good. i want PromQL for the batcher sizing and wait-time histogram. try these: 
- batch_size: sum(rate(batcher_batches_count{model="rw-large-quant"}[5m])) by (batch_size)
- batch_wait_ms_p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batcher_wait_ms_bucket{model="rw-large-quant"}[5m])) by (le))

jena_ml: ran them. p99 wait ~520ms. median wait ~8ms. batch size distribution shows modes at 1 and 16 (we saw more small batches but a second mode at max_batch=16). looks like some requests are waiting for full batches and hitting the batch_timeout window.

alex_support: customer said they saw request id with "held_for_batch": true in response metadata.

sam_oncall: ok actionable theory: continuous batcher default max_wait_ms set to 500ms and max_batch_size 16 for that model profile. with concurrency pattern they sometimes wait almost full 500ms for batch to fill to 16, producing p99 spike. we should test reducing wait and/or prioritizing short-timeout path.

mike_sre: agree. quick mitigation options: 
1) lower batch_timeout_ms to 25-50ms for rw-large-quant route (fastest to patch).
2) add a high-priority route for low-latency customer traffic that disables batching or uses max_batch_size=1.
3) enable adaptive batching experiment: set max_wait_ms=quantile-based (e.g., 95th of recent wait) — more complex.

jena_ml: also check kv cache hit rate — if cache miss causes extra decode time inside batch, it amplifies waiting cost. run: 
- kv_hit_rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits{model="rw-large-quant"}[10m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests{model="rw-large-quant"}[10m]))

mike_sre: kv hit rate is 98% — not the main issue. this is pure batching hold time.

sam_oncall: i'm going to push a canary change to one host pool: patch traffic-table for rw-large-quant to set batcher.max_wait_ms=50 and batcher.max_batch_size=8 for route priority=low. will monitor p99.

alex_support: customer wants ETA for mitigation — they asked for a config change asap.

mike_sre: do quick canary then global. steps: 
1) create a canary patch: 
```
PATCH /config/routes/rw-large-quant
{ "batcher": { "max_wait_ms": 50, "max_batch_size": 8 }, "canary": true }
```
2) route ~2% traffic for 10m.
3) measure p95/p99 vs control (prom queries).

jena_ml: i'll prepare Prom dashboard slices: p50/p95/p99 latency, batch_wait_p99, batch_size_hist, error_rate.

perf_bot: deploy-bot: canary patch applied to pool rw-west-1-canary (2 nodes) by sam_oncall at 03:22 UTC

sam_oncall: canary up. routing sending 2.3% of traffic. watch link: https://dash.redwood/p/rw-large-quant/canary-03-22

mike_sre: initial numbers at +5m: control p99 ~800ms, canary p99 ~380ms. p95 improved from 240ms -> 130ms. batch_wait_p99 for canary ~60ms. :thumbsup:

alex_support: forwarded canary results to customer — they responded cautiously positive. want global fix but worried about throughput cost.

jena_ml: throughput drop negligible for this workload — decreasing batch size increased compute cost ~3% but improved tail greatly. we should propose two-step plan: short-term: lower model profile default max_wait_ms to 50ms and max_batch_size=8 for rw-large-quant; long-term: implement adaptive batching where we measure request intent and route small/low-latency requests into low-batch path automatically.

mike_sre: file a runtime config PR and include rollback. PR checklist: monitoring alerts adjusted, cost impact estimate, opt-in flag. I'll draft.

sam_oncall: rolling global config now in 3 phases: canary -> 25% -> 100% over 30m with automated rollback if p99 > baseline*1.2 or error_rate increases. starting phase 1 at 03:40 UTC.

perf_bot: rollout: phase=25% started at 03:40 UTC by sam_oncall

jena_ml: watch: after 25% rollout p99 dropped system-wide to ~360ms for rw-large-quant. no error spike.

mike_sre: note for postmortem: root cause = mis-tuned continuous-batcher defaults for models with high latency variance; failure mode = long max_wait_ms allowed small requests to block waiting for fill to max_batch_size. mitigation = conservative defaults + adaptive policy + per-customer low-latency bypass.

alex_support: customer happy with interim fix, wants a change advisory and cost estimate.

mike_sre: i'll prepare a short RCA and cost delta: initial estimate 3-5% extra GPU token cost for rw-large-quant across traffic. will attach dashboard slices and canary logs.

jena_ml: next steps: 
- RFC for adaptive-batching (timeline 2 sprints)
- Add metric: fraction_of_requests_held_for_batch (per-route) + alert at 0.5% sustained
- Update model onboarding docs to include recommended batcher defaults based on latency variance.

sam_oncall: tagging incident: INC-2026-0427-batcher-tail. i will close after RCA doc posted.

alex_support: thanks everyone. summarizing for support thread to customer: 1) root cause identified 2) we rolled canary and global config to reduce batch wait 3) monitoring in place 4) long-term RFC queued. cc @customer-774 :thumbsup:

perf_bot: note: no errors or OOMs during rollout. all systems healthy.

mike_sre: leaving this thread. follow-up actions assigned in task tracker.

jena_ml: adding the PromQL snippets and the canary graphs to the RCA doc.

sam_oncall: closing canary pool in 10m if stable.

alex_support: closing thread for now, will reopen if customer reports anything further.
